name: Acroá
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct Jê language of Brazil; only wordlists/subclassification notes (Carvalho & Damulakis 2015); no phonological description found.

readall_conflicts: No source states an Akroá stress rule, so there is no disagreement between statements. The only stress-relevant material is orthographic: Martius's acute accents on the 1819 wordlist (pp. 145-146) fall mostly on the last syllable, or on the syllable before the predicator suffix -de/-te/-ti, which, read as stress marks under the Portuguese-based convention Martius states on pp. 6 and 29 ('den Vocal zu schärfen oder die Sylbe zu betonen'), points to stem-final stress; the convention itself is ambiguous between vowel quality and stress, and it is stated for the Tupi section, not for the Akroá list. Gardner's 'Shódó' with acutes on both syllables does not mark a single stressed syllable. Ribeiro 2012 respells Gardner's word 'Shòdò' with graves, a minor transcription discrepancy with the 1846 page scan.

sources.citation: Martius, Carl Friedrich Philipp von. 1867. Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens, II: Glossaria linguarum Brasiliensium / Wörtersammlung brasilianischer Sprachen. Leipzig: Fleischer. 'Acroa mirim' pp. 145-146; accent convention p. 29
sources.note: The Latin-glossed Acroá-mirim wordlist (~120 items, collected by Spix & Martius 1819) carries acute accents on many forms (<aicrán> head, <aiquá> tooth, <cuipá> manioc, <aimbuttúde> neck, <uöthésu> leaf, <puckúte> lake, <tikkíte> arrow, <aimbösetí> beautiful, <tickáiti> earth, <dewakonó> daughter). No note on Acroá pronunciation; the only statement of the accent's meaning is in the Tupi preface p. 29: the acute 'dient, den Vocal zu schärfen oder die Sylbe zu betonen' (serves to sharpen the vowel or to stress the syllable) — a general orthographic convention, not a rule for Acroá.

sources.citation: Spix, Johann Baptist von & Carl Friedrich Philipp von Martius. 1828. Reise in Brasilien, Bd. 2. München: Lindauer. (Acroá at S. Gonçalo d'Amarante, p. 807 region)
sources.note: scanned heavily garbled; the one legible passage records meeting Geicó and Acroá Indians at S. Gonçalo d'Amarante. No vocabulary or pronunciation note found.
States the language is known only from Martius's short wordlist; cites Spix & Martius 1824, Nikulin 2020, Carvalho & Damulakis 2015. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Nikulin, Andrey. 2020. Proto-Macro-Jê: um estudo reconstrutivo. PhD dissertation, Universidade de Brasília. 595 pp.
sources.note: Akroá appears only in sec. 1.1.1.2 (pp. 13-15): transmission 'foi interrompida antes de as mesmas terem sido amplamente documentadas, restando delas apenas curtas listas vocabulares' (Martius 1867 v. 2 pp. 145-146). No Akroá phonology. For the family he assumes final stress ('Em sílabas tônicas (finais)', p. 234, on Proto-Jê de Goyaz), but this is not applied to Akroá.

sources.citation: de Carvalho, Fernando O. & Gean N. Damulakis. 2015. The structure of Akroá and Xakriabá and their relation to Xavante and Xerente: A contribution to the historical linguistics of the Jê languages. LIAMES 15(1): 17-46. doi:10.20396/liames.v15i1.8641494
sources.note: Nothing on Akroá stress. Sec. 1.2 (p. 21) says the only Akroá data are Martius's non-linguist transcriptions and that phonetic interpretation is largely hopeless; the sole stress remark (p. 26) is that Xerente 'was seemingly subject to a process of vowel deletion (or weakening) prompted by a rightward stress shift', with Akroá forms like <aimbösetí>, <uöthésu> taken as possible evidence of vowel reduction (pp. 28-29) — accent marks on Akroá forms are reproduced but never interpreted.

sources.citation: Ribeiro, Eduardo Rivail. 2012. George Gardner entre os índios do sertão. Blog da Biblioteca Digital Curt Nimuendajú, doc:17
sources.note: Only modern discussion of the Gardner Akroá forms; would say whether Gardner's accent marks are usable.
sources.venue: Blog da Biblioteca Digital Curt Nimuendajú, doc:17

sources.citation: Martius, C. F. P. von. 1867. Beiträge.. II: Wörtersammlung brasilianischer Sprachen, pp. 145-146 — page scan (IA items beitrgezurethn02mart / bub_gb_B3z7W40v4oAC / 10253423bsb)
sources.note: The scanned held held by the project garbles many diacritics (e.g. <aicrän> for <aicrán>); anyone who wants to read Martius's acute accents as a stress record must check them against the scanned page, and compare with the Reise in Brasilien Bd. 2 (1828) appendix if the list was first printed there.

sources.citation: Gardner, George. 1846. Travels in the interior of Brazil, principally through the northern provinces.. during the years 1836-41. London: Reeve. pp. 316-320 (Duro mission, Akroá words ropechedy, shòdò)
sources.note: Second independent eyewitness record of Akroá words (per Carvalho & Damulakis 2015 fn. 18, 24 and Ribeiro 2012); Gardner's English transcription with grave accent <shòdò> could add a second observer's accent marks. Not downloaded today.

sources.citation: Spix, J. B. von & C. F. P. von Martius. 1824. Travels in Brazil, in the years 1817-1820, vol. 2. London: Longman.
sources.note: No Acroá mention at all (the English translation ends before the Piauí leg).
